renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: completeness_contamination
  title: Completeness against contamination
  description: |-
    Each point is a bin: its predicted completeness on the horizontal axis and its predicted contamination on the vertical axis, coloured by binner and sized by genome size. It answers which bins are worth keeping and which binner delivers them.
    How to read: the bottom right corner holds the bins worth naming, and the top half holds chimeric bins with sequences from more than one organism. Compare the colours to see which binner produces more bins in the good corner for this assembly. A large point is a bin with a genome-sized sequence, so a small complete-looking point deserves a second look.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line is a completeness of 50% and the horizontal line a contamination of 10%, the limits of a medium-quality draft in the MIMAG standard. A high-quality draft needs over 90% completeness and under 5% contamination plus rRNA and tRNA genes that CheckM2 does not count. CheckM2 predicts both values with machine-learning models, so they are estimates.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/ and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chklovski/CheckM2/main/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Completeness (%)
    y_title: Contamination (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    quadrants:
      x: 50
      y: 10
      labels:
      - Incomplete and contaminated
      - Contaminated
      - Low quality
      - Medium quality or better
  roles:
    x: completeness
    y: contamination
    label: bin_id
    color: binner
    size: genome_size

- component: advanced_viz
  id: n50_completeness
  title: Contiguity against completeness
  description: |-
    Each point is a bin: the N50 of its contigs on a logarithmic horizontal axis and its predicted completeness on the vertical axis, coloured by assembler and sized by genome size. It answers whether a bin that looks complete is also contiguous.
    How to read: points at the top right are complete and made of long contigs. A complete bin with a small N50 is a collection of fragments that happen to carry the right genes, so it is a weaker genome. Compare the colours to see which assembler gives longer contigs.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a completeness of 50%, the lower limit of a medium-quality draft in the MIMAG standard. No N50 cut-off is drawn, because the standard sets none.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Contig N50 (bp)
    y_title: Completeness (%)
    log_x: true
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 50
    reference_label: 50% complete (MIMAG medium)
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: contig_n50
    y: completeness
    label: bin_id
    color: assembler
    size: genome_size

- component: figure
  title: Completeness distribution per binner
  description: |-
    Each bar counts bins in a completeness band, split by binner. It answers whether a binner returns mostly complete bins or mostly fragments.
    How to read: a binner with its bars at the right produces more complete bins. A pile at low completeness is many partial bins. The MIMAG limit of 50% for a medium-quality draft is drawn on the scatter tile, not here.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median completeness of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of CheckM2.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: completeness
    color: binner
    labels:
      completeness: Completeness (%)
      binner: Binner
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: completeness

- component: figure
  title: Bin quality score by binner and assembler
  description: |-
    Each box is the spread of bin quality scores for one binner and assembler. The score is completeness minus five times contamination, defined by this catalog module. It answers which binner and assembler combination yields the best bins.
    How to read: a higher box means better bins, and a box reaching below zero holds bins whose contamination outweighs their completeness. With few bins per group the boxes are only indicative, so open the table for the individual values.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median bin quality score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of CheckM2.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: binner
    y: quality_score
    color: assembler
    labels:
      binner: Binner
      quality_score: Bin quality score
      assembler: Assembler
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: quality_score

- component: card
  id: tier_donut
  title: Bins by quality tier
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of bins, the second number counts the samples they come from, and the ring splits the bins by quality tier. It answers how many bins reach each tier.
    How to read: a ring dominated by high and medium quality means a good binning run. Contaminated is this catalog's label for bins with 10% contamination or more.
    Lines and annotations: the tiers use the MIMAG completeness and contamination limits: high is over 90% complete and under 5% contaminated, medium at least 50% and under 10%, and low under 50% and under 10%. The rRNA and tRNA requirements of a full high-quality draft are not checked here.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: quality_tier
  caption: bins, by quality tier

- component: card
  title: Completeness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median predicted completeness of the bins, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much of a genome a typical bin holds.
    How to read: a median near 100% means the bins are nearly whole genomes. A wide box means some bins are fragments, so open the scatter to see them. The MIMAG limits of 50% and 90% are drawn on the scatter tile.
  column: completeness
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Contamination
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median predicted contamination of the bins, with the highest bin below it, and the strip counts the bins under and over the limit. It answers how many bins stay clean enough to use.
    How to read: a low median with a high maximum means most bins are clean and a few are chimeras, which should be removed or refined. Contamination is the share of marker-like content found more than once.
    Lines and annotations: the limit is a contamination of 10%, the upper bound of a medium-quality draft in the MIMAG standard, which asks for under 5% for a high-quality one.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  column: contamination
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 10.0
  threshold_direction: max
  caption: bins under and over 10% contamination

- component: card
  title: Best bin score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest quality score of any bin, and the box shows the spread over all bins. The score is completeness minus five times contamination, defined by this catalog module. It answers how good the best bin is and how far the others lag.
    How to read: a best score far above the median means a few good bins among many poor ones. A score below zero means contamination outweighs completeness.
  column: quality_score
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: best bin, with the spread of all bins

- component: card
  title: Genome size
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median bin genome size in base pairs, with the smallest and largest below it, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how large the recovered genomes are.
    How to read: sizes cover a wide range because bins can be fragments or whole genomes. A bin far larger than its neighbours may merge several organisms, so compare it with its contamination.
  column: genome_size
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: genome size of every bin

- component: card
  title: Coding density
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean coding density, the fraction of the genome that codes for proteins, with the lowest and highest bin below it, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers whether the bins look like typical genomes.
    How to read: prokaryotic genomes are usually densely coding, so a low value suggests fragmented or non-coding content. No cut-off is drawn, because CheckM2 and the MIMAG standard set none for it.
  column: coding_density
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: coding density of every bin

- component: table
  title: Bin quality table
  description: |-
    Each row is a bin with its predicted completeness and contamination, quality score and tier, and the assembly statistics CheckM2 reports: coding density, contig N50, genome size, GC content and gene count. It answers the exact values behind every tile of this view.
    How to read: sort by quality score to rank the bins, or filter by binner to compare methods.
